snippet.title: Elephant Herd Crosses Railway Track in Hojai, Rajdhani Express Halted Safely
snippet.description:
Guwahati, August 19: The Down Rajdhani Express was stopped temporarily on Wednesday morning after an elephant herd crossed the railway track at Hawaipur in Assam’s Hojai district, allowing the animals to pass safely.

According to sources, the train was halted at Km 167/8 as the elephant herd crossed the tracks at Hawaipur under Lanka Range of the Nagaon South Division.

Assam Minister Jayanta Malla Baruah also shared the incident on social media, describing it as an unexpected halt that allowed the “adorable giants” to cross safely.
He said the alert actions of Assam Forest Department personnel, the loco pilot and the Lumding Railway Control Room ensured the safe passage of the elephant herd, following which the train resumed its journey.

The incident highlights the continued efforts of forest personnel and railway authorities to prevent human-wildlife conflict and ensure the safe movement of elephants across railway tracks in Assam.

snippet.title: 24 Oras Express: August 19, 2026 [HD]
snippet.description:
Narito ang mga maiinit na balita sa 24 Oras Express ngayong Miyerkules, August 19, 2026.


- Bahagi ng QC at Camanava, binaha;may mga motoristang stranded

- Bahay malapit sa ilog, gumuho

- Hanggang dibdib na baha, binabangka na; nag-iwan ng basura nang humupa

- Ilang lugar, nag-anunsiyong walang pasok bukas

- DILG: Hinatid ng sasakyan ang 14yo shooter kaya 'di nainspeksyon ng campus security

- Ateneo De Zamboanga University, nagluluksa; DSWD, nagsasagawa ng post-trauma informed care

- Ilang menor de edad, inokopa ang bahagi ng kalsada at nagbatuhan

- Pagiging bahain ng ilang barangay, ilang dekada nang problema sa bayan

- Sparkle stars, nakisaya sa mga dugong Pinoy sa 'Taste of Manila' event sa Toronto, Canada

- Government offices, magpapatupad pa rin ng alternative work arrangements

- Matagal na paghupa ng baha sa ilang bahagi ng Metro Manila, namerwisyo

- Pagsapubliko sa biyahe niya, pinalagan ng VP; Palasyo: walang mali sa pagsapubliko niyan

- Epekto ng Habagat, posibleng umabot pa hanggang weekend o sa susunod ng linggo; 3 bagyo, mino-monitor sa paligid ng bansa

- Maulang panahon na nararanasan City of Pines, inaasahang magpapatuloy hanggang long weekend

- VP Duterte, dumalaw sa pamilya ng biktima at mga survivor ng pamamaril

- Sen. Padilla, nagpost ng litrato nila nina Senators Go at Mark Villar sa Senate lounge habang 'nakikinig sa trial'

- 22 leptospirosis cases sa San Lazaro Hospital, inaasahang tataas pa; 3 ang malalalang kaso

- Guteza, binawi ang salaysay na nag-deliver siya ng male-maletang pera sa bahay ni ex-Speaker Romualdez; pakana umano ito nina Sen. Marcoleta at ex-Rep. Defensor

- Naunang utos ng ERC na bawiin ang provisional authority to operate ng sipcor, binaliktad ng CA

- GMA Chief Marketing Officer Lizelle Maralag, kinilala ng AD Standards Council

- Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, kinumpleto na ang mga miyembro ng minorya sa mga komite ng Senado

- Jennylyn Mercado at Rhian Ramos, magbabalik sa 'Bubble Gang'

- Pangontra-baha ng isang establisimyento, dagdag sa maraming DIY flood control

snippet.title: Dubai Room-Sharing Rules Change: Heavy Fines for Violations
snippet.description:
Dubai has introduced new regulations for shared housing, requiring units used as shared accommodation to obtain an official permit. Only the property owner or a licensed establishment can legally lease a shared housing unit, while tenants cannot independently rent out rooms or parts of the property.

Violations can result in fines ranging from AED 500 to AED 500,000, while repeat violations within one year can lead to fines of up to AED 1 million. The law takes effect 180 days after its publication in the Official Gazette, with the effective date expected around August 26, 2026.

snippet.title: Imran Khan to Hospital? | Government Plays Its Legal Card | Bilawal Meets PTI Leaders
snippet.description:
#ImranKhan #SupremeCourt #ShifaHospital

SC orders moving jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital for medical checkup


The Supreme Court directed the relevant authorities on Tuesday to shift jailed PTI founder Imran Khan to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital for a complete medical checkup in the next few days.

A three-member SC bench, headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibrahim, issued the ruling on several petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation as well as his meetings with family members.

Imran had approached the SC in May, seeking directions for his transfer to Shifa International Hospital, access to his personal physicians, family members and counsel, and the provision of his medical details to his family.

The court today ordered the constitution of a medical board at Shifa International Hospital to examine the former premier, and directed jail authorities to ensure weekly meetings between Imran and his family members, as well as telephonic conversations with his sons.

The court observed that since Imran’s health was at stake, and as the right to life and access to medical facilities were rights enshrined under Article 9 of the Constitution, this order was being issued.

“Mindful of this fundamental right, we are issuing this order to ensure health and safety of the prisoner,” Justice Waheed said.

The court issued its directives after Additional Attorney General (AAG) Chaudhry Aamir Rehman opposed the suggestion to shift the prisoner to Shifa International Hospital.

The AAG contended that the prisoner could not be shifted to the private hospital at the moment, and that no notice to this effect had been issued to the government.

Nevertheless, the AAG participated in the hearing, observed Justice Waheed while dictating the order.

The court-ordered medical board is to include a cardiologist, general medicine specialist, eye specialist as well as Dr Faisal Sultan, the personal physician of Imran. Petitioner Dr Uzma Khan, the sister of Imran, will also be associated with the medical examination.

As assured by the petitioner, the court ordered all necessary expenses of a complete medical checkup were to be borne by the petitioner’s family and attendants.

The court order also has several caveats. The family members of the prisoner, and the doctors or a lawyer associated with the case must not share the medical report prepared by the hospital’s medical board with the media or the public at large, or use it for any political purposes.

In case of a violation of the court order, the facility extended by the SC will be withdrawn forthwith, the order cautioned, adding that if the government believes the facility is being misused, they will be at liberty to move an appropriate application in this regard.

Likewise, the petitioner’s side can also file an application in case of reluctance on the part of the government, the order stated.

Additionally, Imran’s party, family members and lawyers associated with the case must also ensure that no public gathering or rally will be arranged outside the precincts of Shifa Hospital, the order said.

The Court also ordered weekly meetings between the family members and the prisoner. Telephonic conversations with the sons of Imran will also be part of the order.

Govt files review plea against SC ruling to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital, terms it 'discriminatory'

SLAMABAD: The federal government on Wednesday filed a petition in the Supreme Court, seeking a review and recall of the SC order to shift incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan to Islamabad’s Shifa Inte­rn­ati­onal Hospital for medical examination and treatment.

The government’s review petition, filed by Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik on behalf of the federal capital’s chief commissioner a day after the SC’s ruling, termed the interim order “discriminatory”.

The petition, a copy stated that the order was “in excess of jurisdiction” and, therefore, “liable to be reviewed”.

The plea further stated that the order suffers from errors of law floating on the surface of the record”.

snippet.title: UAE imposes indefinite trade embargo on Iran over alleged missile attacks
snippet.description:
The United Arab Emirates has announced it is imposing an indefinite trade embargo on Iran, with the Foreign Ministry saying Tehran is "undermining regional and international peace and security." The announcement follows an earlier statement by the UAE's Defence Ministry that it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards the country. Iran's Foreign Ministry has rejected the accusations, calling them baseless and saying the incident is a "false flag operation." In an interview with Al Jazeera, retired General Mark Kimmitt, a former US Assistant Secretary of State, said Dubai is the largest seller of imported goods to Iran, exceeding China and Turkey, with one-third of Iran's imports coming from the UAE. He said the embargo could be "even more significant than the embargo being put on by the United States" and warned that Iran "might go to war with the UAE because of it." President Donald Trump posted that the Strait of Hormuz is open, while the US naval blockade of Iran remains in place.
